note.text: The initial straight corridor is narrow and hugs the left rail near the bend entry, causing the trailer rear-left to repeatedly clip the inside barrier. When reversing, initiate a rightward offset early so the trailer enters the bend away from the left rail. Reversing into a rightward curve requires negative hitch angle, but over-angling pushes the rear-left corner outward into the wall. Keep hitch angles shallow and react early rather than making large corrections. When pulling forward, steer gently to avoid swinging the vehicle front-right corner into the outside rail.

note.text: The course curves left around ten metres in, causing the trailer rear-right to scrape repeatedly if kept centred. Steer right early to swing the trailer left well before the bend. When unpinning forward, keep steering very gentle to avoid clipping the front corners against the opposite rail. Reversing speed should stay around half speed to allow the wheels enough time to steer. Alternate mirror checks or use a wide backward gaze to track both side clearances continuously.

note.text: We repeatedly struck the left rail because the course layout curves or has the target bay placed far to the right, leaving huge clearance on the right but an extreme pinch on the left. Right from the start, actively steer and bias the rig toward the wide right space rather than following the starting lane heading. Keep reversing speed very gentle. The mower has an ultra-short wheelbase and hitch, reacting extremely fast to steering adjustments, so apply small smooth inputs and track the actual target bearing rather than hugging the narrow left barrier.

note.text: Reversing straight into the corner worked well, but sharp steering during the ninety-degree turn swung the tractor's front overhang into the outer rails. Priority: maintain a gentle hitch angle through the turn so the cab does not sweep wide, and clamp front wheel angles strictly. Once the trailer enters the bay corridor, track the painted bay corners visible on the rear camera to centre the rig smoothly. Tip for this long semi combination: small steering adjustments go a long way; large wheel locks cause the front corners to clip barriers before the trailer responds.
